props.segment: Keys on the Tick: A Run Cycle and a Wolf Lunge

beats.heading: What got built
beats.narration_text: Two clips: a run and a lunge. The lesson: animation here is timing, not drawing — keys on the physics tick the game reads, with gameplay pinned before the first key.

props.text:
Two clips:
a run, a lunge.
Animation
is drawing.

beats.heading: The game and its two clips
beats.narration_text: The game: walker-magic, a two-D side-scroller — a fire mage, a cave, a wolf. Two new clips. The mage's run is a Sprite2D frame track, and it loops. The wolf's lunge is a cutout rig keyed as resource text, and it commits: once the dash starts, a hit no longer cancels it.

shot.visual_intent: The game and its two clips

show.event: The game and its two clips

beats.heading: The run, in play
beats.narration_text: Now the real game, played by scripted input — real key presses, real engine output. The mage runs, four cells at ten a second, stops, runs, jumps the pit and lands. At quarter speed: on the landing tick, the run starts again at cell zero.

beats.heading: The lunge in both facings, in play
beats.narration_text: The wolf. It growls where it first sees her, crouching for thirty-one ticks; she steps back, and the lunge misses, trailing orange ghosts. She runs past; it turns and lunges right. One clip, both facings: code flips the Facing node, the clip keys the rig inside.

shot.visual_intent: The lunge in both facings, in play

show.event: The lunge in both facings, in play

beats.heading: A hit in the growl cancels the lunge
beats.narration_text: Now an interrupt in each phase, from real clicks. First, the growl: the fireball leaves on growl tick two and lands on tick twenty-one. The lunge is cancelled — recovery on the hit tick, clip frame fifty-three, and the hitbox never arms.

shot.visual_intent: A hit in the growl cancels the lunge

show.event: A hit in the growl cancels the lunge

beats.heading: A hit in the lunge does not cancel
beats.narration_text: Second, the lunge. A click on growl tick sixteen; the fireball lands four ticks into the dash, at clip frame thirty-five. The wolf flashes and loses HP, but the dash runs its full twenty-two ticks, and recovery starts at fifty-three as usual.

shot.visual_intent: A hit in the lunge does not cancel

show.event: A hit in the lunge does not cancel

beats.heading: A hit in the recovery: HP only
beats.narration_text: Third, the recovery: a click during the dash, a hit on recovery tick five, clip frame fifty-eight. Only HP changes; the wolf still stands all thirty-six ticks. Every phase here is read from the frame log, not by eye.

shot.visual_intent: A hit in the recovery: HP only

show.event: A hit in the recovery: HP only

beats.heading: Idea 1: what a clip is
beats.narration_text: Idea one, in the author's words: a clip is a timeline of keys on named node properties; a track resolves its target from a NodePath string at run time — here, Sprite2D colon frame. That a wrong path is skipped with no error is, in the author's own note, an understanding, not a measurement. What was measured: the read-back catches it.

beats.heading: Clip 1: the sheet and its slicing
beats.narration_text: The sheet that track reads: four cells of sixty-two by sixty-nine, four by one — contact, down, passing, up. Drawn in the Gemini app from the author's prompt and own sprite, then cleaned onto the author's palette.

shot.visual_intent: Clip 1: the sheet and its slicing

show.event: Clip 1: the sheet and its slicing

beats.heading: The frame track that reads it (code)
beats.narration_text: The frame track: discrete, cells zero to three at zero, point one, point two and point three seconds, looping at point four. Step: point one, ten frames a second. No duplicate across the wrap; the last gap equals the others.

beats.heading: The run, cell by cell (result)
beats.narration_text: Tick by tick, in the capture: six, six, six, seven ticks per cell on entry, then five, six, six, seven each loop — the clip wraps on the tick it reaches point four. The read-back: seventeen of seventeen.

beats.heading: Idea 2: one authority
beats.narration_text: Idea two, in the author's words: one authority means each animated property is written by exactly one player; with two, they overwrite each other every frame and the picture twitches or falls out of step. Here, the state machine only calls play, and a test scans every script for other writers.

beats.heading: Land, run, cell zero
beats.narration_text: In the capture: falling, then on the landing tick, run — from cell zero, not wherever the last run left off. Eleven structure checks agree.

beats.heading: Idea 4: feel designed in frames
beats.narration_text: Idea four, in the author's words: designing feel in frames means splitting an action into startup, active and recovery frame counts, not by dragging keys by eye. Startup, the growl, frames zero to thirty: hitbox off, and a hit cancels. Active, the lunge, thirty-one to fifty-two: the game reads the hitbox; dodge — a hit doesn't cancel. Recovery, fifty-three to eighty-eight: the wolf stands; punish freely.

beats.heading: The keys built from the table (code)
beats.narration_text: In the scene file, the keys built from that table: frames zero, twenty-five, thirty-one, thirty-seven, fifty-three, sixty-five and eighty-nine, each over sixty — crouch, stretch, overshoot. The clip's step is one sixtieth of a second.

beats.narration_text: At each phase boundary, in a fixture strip and in play: neutral at zero, the crouch held at thirty-one, the stretch held at fifty-three, and back to patrol at eighty-nine. The read-back: eighteen of eighteen — every track resolves, every key within half a frame.

beats.heading: Idea 3: two clocks, measured
beats.narration_text: Idea three, in the author's words: the two clocks are the variable-rate process clock and the fixed-step physics clock; my state machines, the hitbox and both clip players run on the physics clock. Measured: clip time equals phase time on all eighty-nine ticks — but the hitbox is read one tick late, frames thirty-two to fifty-three against thirty-one to fifty-two. A sixtieth of a second.

beats.heading: The change (code)
beats.narration_text: The one behaviour change, in code: a hit that leaves HP during the growl sends the wolf to recover and seeks the clip to the recovery section. Every other phase only loses HP.

beats.heading: What the pin saw (result)
beats.narration_text: Gameplay was pinned before any clip: eight scenarios, every tick, three rates; adding and wiring the clips changed nothing. This change did, from tick twenty-four: growl to recover, no lunge. Kill changed too; its first hit lands in a growl. Played, accepted, re-pinned.

beats.heading: Edges: before, on and after every boundary
beats.narration_text: The edges: real clicks timed to land one tick before, on, and after every phase boundary. A hit on a boundary is handled before the wolf's update, so it follows the phase before. Cancel in the growl, none in the lunge, HP only after. Twenty-five of twenty-five, at three rates.

beats.heading: Broken on purpose: M1 to M4
beats.narration_text: Broken on purpose: four published mutations, each in a worktree. A misspelt property on a lunge track: exit one — track problems reports FrontPivot has no property rotaton. The run's loop set to none: exit one. A frame key past the sheet: exit one. The import cache deleted and rebuilt: every read-back passes, proving only that the clips don't depend on it.

shot.visual_intent: Broken on purpose: M1 to M4

show.event: Broken on purpose: M1 to M4

beats.heading: What the read-backs proved, and what they cannot
beats.narration_text: The read-backs proved structure: run seventeen, lunge eighteen, flicker twelve, structure eleven, no failures — tracks resolve, keys within half a frame, step and modes as the brief says. What no headless run shows: whether either motion reads or feels committed, or whether the cycle wraps cleanly to the eye. That took the author, in play.

shot.visual_intent: What the read-backs proved, and what they cannot

show.event: What the read-backs proved, and what they cannot

beats.heading: Claude against the author
beats.narration_text: Claude against the author. Claude estimated a two-point-six to three-point-three pixel step at the waist seam; the author saw none. Claude's run r1 hit every predicted hat row; the author rejected it in play. Claude read the visual upgrades as matching; the author found them not noticeable. And the slips the author recorded: an amended local commit, and a backup kept one folder above the assignment for a few seconds.

beats.heading: Uncertain, and the next step
beats.narration_text: Still uncertain: the planted foot slides; the growl window is a fifth of a second, by choice; the hitbox is read a sixtieth late; and a fresh clone of the submitted commit can only come after this film. The author's next step: in-betweens for the planted foot, in the final project.

beats.heading: Who did what; the sheet; the revision
beats.narration_text: Who did what. The author chose both clips, the interrupt rule and the window, made the run sheet in the Gemini app — model shown as 4 Hydrogen, under Google's terms — and judged everything in play. Claude Code built the pin, clips, tests, mutations and this film; Claude in chat drafted the documents. Source shown: a d seven nine three five f.

shot.visual_intent: Who did what; the sheet; the revision

show.event: Who did what; the sheet; the revision

beats.heading: Verdict
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Built: two clips, each owned by one animation player on the physics tick, and one designed interrupt. Measured: a pin the clips never moved, edges at every boundary, three mutations caught. Judged in play by the author. Open: the sliding foot.

artifactLines: Built: the run clip (4 cells, 10 fps, step 0.1, LOOP_LINEAR, discrete) and the lunge rig and clip (89 frames, step 1/60, LOOP_NONE), each owned by one AnimationPlayer on the physics callback; the growl cancel.

Measured: pin 16 / 0 at 30, 60, 144, unchanged by the clips; the change re-pinned after play (ff71bbb); edges 25 / 0 at 30, 60, 144; read-backs 17, 18, 12, 11 / 0; M1–M3 caught, M4 (fresh import) passes.
Judged by the author in play: run r2 kept (r1 rejected), the three phases and an interrupt in each, the 0.2 s growl window kept.
Open: in-between frames so the planted foot stops sliding; the hitbox read 1/60 s after the clip’s active section; a fresh clone at the submitted commit.

beats.heading: Your Turn
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt: Please use Walker to add in-between frames to my mage's run so the planted foot stops sliding. First predict, in pixels, how far the body moves while one cell is held at a hundred and ten pixels a second and ten frames a second; then measure the foot in a windowed Movie Maker strip, and show the behaviour pin still matches tick for tick. Liam, in for Bear.
